description:
What it is: Benes permutation network: Realizes arbitrary permutations through two butterfly halves of 2x2 switches whose settings are held in configuration registers.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
RiftCore-style issue-lane shuffler: a pipelined 8x8 Benes network (5 stages of 4 2x2 switches = 20 switch bits) that permutes eight 64-bit operand words from rename lanes to execution ports. Switch settings come from a 256-entry permutation table, so each beat can pick a different routing.

Inputs:
- clk, rst.
- en: the idle input. When en is low, every register holds.
- in_valid; in_data[8][64]; in_sel[7:0], which picks the table entry.
- cfg_we, cfg_addr[7:0], cfg_bits[19:0]: table write port.

State registers:
- cfg_tab[256][20]: permutation table.
- stage_cfg[5][4]: settings latched per stage for the beat in flight.
- data_pipe[5][8][64]: words held between stages.
- valid_pipe[4:0]: one valid bit per stage.
- inflight[63:0]: number of beats currently in the network.
- beats_done[63:0]: retired-beat counter, not used in P.
- armed (1 bit): sticky; set the first time cfg_we is high while en is high, never cleared.

Behaviour when en is high:
- cfg_we writes cfg_tab[cfg_addr].
- valid_pipe shifts left: valid_pipe <= {valid_pipe[3:0], in_valid}.
- data_pipe and stage_cfg advance one stage. Each stage swaps or passes its lane pairs according to its 4 bits, wired as a Benes network (butterfly, then inverse butterfly).
- inflight <= inflight + in_valid - valid_pipe[4].
- beats_done increments when valid_pipe[4] is set.
- Reset clears everything.

Relation R (holds by construction): inflight == popcount(valid_pipe). The counter rises exactly when a valid bit enters and falls exactly when one leaves stage 4.

Property P (after-Q bounded existence, at most 5):
always @(posedge clk) assert (!armed || inflight <= 64'd5);
The bound 5 is the network depth, far below the 2^64 the width allows, so it is a real fact about reachable states.

Counterexample to induction (state satisfying P, violating R):
- armed = 1, inflight = 5, valid_pipe = 5'b00000; the other registers are arbitrary.
- P holds because 5 <= 5.
- R fails because popcount(valid_pipe) = 0 but inflight = 5.
- With en low the state is held indefinitely, so it is consistent for any induction depth.
- Then raise en with in_valid = 1. Since valid_pipe[4] = 0, inflight becomes 6 and P is violated.
- k-induction alone cannot exclude this state. Given R, inflight <= popcount of 5 bits <= 5, and P follows immediately.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. A one-entry output holding register (g_valid/g_data) sits between the shuffler and the perfmon.

description:
What it is: Character display generator: Renders text by fetching character codes and font rows, keeping a character memory, font ROM, and row/column counters.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module tplan_banner_gen: a character display generator that renders a 24-character test-plan banner, such as 'TB PASS: RISC-V ALU', in the HDLGen wizard style. It walks a 24-entry character memory and indexes a combinational 8-row font ROM. Rendering follows a three-step chain: arm, then start, then finish.

Inputs: clk, rst_n, en (idle input; when en=0 every register holds its value), arm_req, start_req, abort_req, and wr_en/wr_addr[4:0]/wr_data[63:0] for loading the character memory.

State registers:
- char_mem[0:23], 64 bits each; the low 8 bits are the character code.
- col_cnt[63:0] and row_cnt[63:0].
- frame_cnt[63:0].
- phase[1:0], encoded IDLE=0, ARMED=1, RUN=2, FIN=3.
- arm_seen[0:0], start_seen[0:0] and done[0:0].
- before_abort[0:0], which resets to 1.
- pix_row[7:0], the current font row output.

Behaviour, applied only while en=1:
- IDLE with arm_req: phase becomes ARMED, arm_seen=1, done=0.
- ARMED with start_req: phase becomes RUN, start_seen=1, and col_cnt and row_cnt are cleared.
- In RUN, each cycle fetches char_mem[col_cnt][7:0] and font row row_cnt into pix_row, then increments col_cnt.
- When col_cnt reaches 23 it wraps to 0 and row_cnt increments.
- When col_cnt==23 and row_cnt==7: phase becomes FIN, done=1 and frame_cnt increments.
- FIN with arm_req re-arms.
- abort_req returns phase to IDLE and clears arm_seen, start_seen and done in the same cycle. It also clears before_abort, which is the scope event R.

Relation R, which holds by construction:
- phase==ARMED implies arm_seen.
- phase is RUN or FIN implies arm_seen and start_seen.
- done implies phase==FIN.
- start_seen implies arm_seen.

Property P (chain precedence, before abort, $rose edge style). The antecedents are before_abort and $rose(done):
  assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) before_abort && $rose(done) |-> arm_seen && start_seen && phase==FIN);
In words: while no abort has ever happened, whenever the finish flag rises, the arm and start steps must already have been recorded.

Counterexample to induction, which satisfies P but violates R:
- phase=RUN, arm_seen=0, start_seen=0, done=0.
- col_cnt=23, row_cnt=7, before_abort=1, with arbitrary char_mem and frame_cnt.
- P holds vacuously in this state because done does not rise.
- The state can be held indefinitely with en=0, since every register holds and done stays 0. This defeats k-induction for any depth k.

One step with en=1 and abort_req=0 moves the design to phase=FIN with done=1. That makes $rose(done) true while arm_seen=0 and start_seen=0, so P is violated. Supplying R as a strengthening invariant excludes the state, because RUN would force arm_seen and start_seen, and P then becomes 1-inductive.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. A new sub-module tplan_seq_ctrl, instantiated once as u_seq, is a start sequencer with its own CSR bank. Writes to the unused addresses wr_addr 24..31 reach it.
2. A new sub-module tplan_launch_sched, instantiated once as u_lnch, is a slot-aligned launch scheduler. Its CSR bank sits at wr_addr 28..31 (csr_addr 4..7), which u_seq ignores.

description:
What it is: SPI chip-select sequencer: Asserts and deasserts individual slave-select lines with programmable setup, hold and inter-transfer delays, keeping a selected-slave register, a delay counter and a sequencing state register.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module toast_spi_cs_seq: a memory-mapped SPI chip-select sequencer peripheral, as a Toast RV32I core would expose over MMIO. Software pushes transfer descriptors into a 24-entry queue. Each descriptor holds a 5-bit slave index (0..23) and a 128-bit data word. The sequencer pops a descriptor, asserts that slave's select line, waits a programmable setup delay, then shifts out 128 bits. It then waits a hold delay, deasserts the select line, and waits an inter-transfer gap.

Inputs: clk, rst, en (when en is low every state register holds its value), push, push_slv[4:0], push_data[127:0], and the delay registers cfg_setup[7:0], cfg_hold[7:0], cfg_gap[7:0].

State registers:
- st[2:0]: IDLE, SETUP, XFER, HOLD, GAP.
- sel[4:0]: the selected slave.
- dly[7:0]: delay counter.
- bitcnt[6:0]: shift counter.
- cs_vec[23:0]: active-high select lines; the output is cs_n = ~cs_vec.
- shreg[127:0]: shift register.
- Queue: q_slv[0:23][4:0], q_dat[0:23][127:0], wptr[4:0], rptr[4:0], count[4:0] (24 entries, so the pointers wrap at 23).

Behaviour (all updates only when en is high):
- In IDLE or at the end of GAP, if count != 0: pop the head entry, set sel to q_slv[rptr], set cs_vec <= cs_vec | (24'b1 << q_slv[rptr]), load shreg and set dly <= cfg_setup, then go to SETUP.
- SETUP counts dly down to 0, then goes to XFER with bitcnt = 127.
- XFER shifts one bit per cycle until bitcnt reaches 0, then goes to HOLD with dly = cfg_hold.
- At the end of HOLD: cs_vec <= cs_vec & ~(24'b1 << sel), dly <= cfg_gap, then go to GAP.
- When GAP expires with an empty queue, go to IDLE.
- Reset clears everything.

The select update is a read-modify-write of cs_vec rather than a fresh one-hot assignment. This is why the invariant is only maintained by construction and is not locally evident.

Relation R (holds by construction):
- When st is SETUP, XFER or HOLD: cs_vec == (24'b1 << sel) and sel < 24.
- When st is IDLE or GAP: cs_vec == 24'b0.

Property P (absence of two simultaneous slave selects, global, guarded):
always @(posedge clk) if (st != ST_IDLE) assert ($onehot0(cs_vec));

Counterexample to induction (satisfies P, violates R):
- st = GAP, dly = 1, sel = 5, cs_vec = 24'h000008 (bit 3 stale), count = 1, and q_slv[rptr] = 7.
- P holds, because cs_vec is onehot0.
- R is violated, because cs_vec should be 0 in GAP.
- With en low this state is held indefinitely, so a k-induction prefix of any length satisfies P.
- When en rises, dly reaches 0, the queue pops slave 7, and st moves to SETUP with cs_vec = 24'h000088.
- Two select lines are now asserted with st != IDLE, so P fails.

Giving the prover R excludes the stale bit, and P then becomes inductive.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. A new sub-module toast_spi_cs_keeper (instance u_keeper) adds a chip-select continuation (CS merge/linger) controller.
2. A new sub-module toast_spi_cs_csr (instance u_csr) adds an in-band control and status register bank. A frame pushed with the reserved slave index 31 is decoded as a control word instead of being queued.

added: A new sub-module toast_spi_rec_guard (instance u_recg) enforces a per-slave CS recovery time. When one slave's chip select is released, that slave may not be selected again until its recovery window has elapsed.

- armed (1 bit): sticky; set the first time cfg_we is high while en is high, never cleared.

Behaviour when en is high:
- cfg_we writes cfg_tab[cfg_addr].
- valid_pipe shifts left: valid_pipe <= {valid_pipe[3:0], in_valid}.
- data_pipe and stage_cfg advance one stage. Each stage swaps or passes its lane pairs according to its 4 bits, wired as a Benes network (butterfly, then inverse butterfly).
- inflight <= inflight + in_valid - valid_pipe[4].
- beats_done increments when valid_pipe[4] is set.
- Reset clears everything.

Relation R (holds by construction): inflight == popcount(valid_pipe). The counter rises exactly when a valid bit enters and falls exactly when one leaves stage 4.

Property P (after-Q bounded existence, at most 5):
always @(posedge clk) assert (!armed || inflight <= 64'd5);
The bound 5 is the network depth, far below the 2^64 the width allows, so it is a real fact about reachable states.

Counterexample to induction (state satisfying P, violating R):
- armed = 1, inflight = 5, valid_pipe = 5'b00000; the other registers are arbitrary.
- P holds because 5 <= 5.
- R fails because popcount(valid_pipe) = 0 but inflight = 5.
- With en low the state is held indefinitely, so it is consistent for any induction depth.
- Then raise en with in_valid = 1. Since valid_pipe[4] = 0, inflight becomes 6 and P is violated.
- k-induction alone cannot exclude this state. Given R, inflight <= popcount of 5 bits <= 5, and P follows immediately.

description:
What it is: Elliptic-curve point adder/doubler: Performs point addition and doubling in projective or Jacobian coordinates by sequencing field multiplications and additions, holding the X, Y, Z coordinate registers of the operands and temporaries.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module ec_jdbl_seq: a 32-bit Jacobian point-doubling/addition sequencer. It has a 16-entry x 32-bit register file `rf[0:15]`. Entries 0-2 hold X1,Y1,Z1, entries 3-5 hold X2,Y2,Z2, and entries 6-15 hold temporaries. Field arithmetic is modulo p = 2^32-5.

Inputs: clk, rst, en (when low, every register holds), arm, start, clr, sel_add (add vs double), and wr_addr/wr_data (operand load while not running).

State registers:
- armed (1)
- started (1)
- done (1)
- pre_clr (1): starts at 1, cleared the first cycle en && clr.
- step [31:0]: micro-op index; 0 means not running.
- acc [31:0]: field multiply/add result.
- rf (16 x 32)

Behaviour when en is high:
- arm sets armed.
- If start && armed && step==0, then step<=1 and started<=1.
- While step != 0, each cycle performs micro-op number step from a fixed 11-op schedule, for example T6=Y1*Y1, T7=X1*T6, T8=X1*X1 and so on. Each op reads two rf entries, writes acc into a temporary, and does step<=step+1.
- When step==11, it writes back X3,Y3,Z3 into rf[0..2], sets done<=1 and step<=0.
- clr clears armed, started and done but deliberately leaves step and rf alone (soft clear of handshake flags only). Thus after a clr a run already in progress can finish with started=0. This is why the property is scoped before the first clr.

Relation R (holds by construction while pre_clr):
- (step != 0) -> (started && armed)
- started -> armed
- done -> started

Property P (Chain Precedence arm -> start -> finish, scope before clr; pre_clr listed in antecedents):
  always @(*) assert (!pre_clr || !done || (started && armed));

Counterexample-to-induction state:
- pre_clr=1, armed=1, started=0, done=0, step=10, en=0.
- P holds because done=0.
- R is violated because step != 0 while started=0.
- With en low the state is frozen indefinitely, so arbitrarily long stuttering prefixes all satisfy P. Plain k-induction therefore cannot exclude it for any k.

On the next en=1 cycle with clr=0:
- step goes 10 -> 11.
- One more cycle sets done=1 with started=0, violating P.

Supplying R as a lemma makes P 1-inductive. step==0 is guaranteed whenever started is 0, so done can only be set after the start event, which itself required armed.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. A two-slot result FIFO (32-bit data slots q_d, per-slot valid bits q_v, write/read pointers q_wr/q_rd and an occupancy count q_cnt) captures A's o_acc on each rising edge of A's sticky o_done and presents the head slot, zero-extended, to B's chunk with vld = (q_cnt != 0).

What it is: Character display generator: Renders text by fetching character codes and font rows, keeping a character memory, font ROM, and row/column counters.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module tplan_banner_gen: a character display generator that renders a 24-character test-plan banner, such as 'TB PASS: RISC-V ALU', in the HDLGen wizard style. It walks a 24-entry character memory and indexes a combinational 8-row font ROM. Rendering follows a three-step chain: arm, then start, then finish.

State registers:
- char_mem[0:23], 64 bits each; the low 8 bits are the character code.
- col_cnt[63:0] and row_cnt[63:0].
- frame_cnt[63:0].
- phase[1:0], encoded IDLE=0, ARMED=1, RUN=2, FIN=3.
- arm_seen[0:0], start_seen[0:0] and done[0:0].
- before_abort[0:0], which resets to 1.
- pix_row[7:0], the current font row output.

Behaviour, applied only while en=1:
- IDLE with arm_req: phase becomes ARMED, arm_seen=1, done=0.
- ARMED with start_req: phase becomes RUN, start_seen=1, and col_cnt and row_cnt are cleared.
- In RUN, each cycle fetches char_mem[col_cnt][7:0] and font row row_cnt into pix_row, then increments col_cnt.
- When col_cnt reaches 23 it wraps to 0 and row_cnt increments.
- When col_cnt==23 and row_cnt==7: phase becomes FIN, done=1 and frame_cnt increments.
- FIN with arm_req re-arms.
- abort_req returns phase to IDLE and clears arm_seen, start_seen and done in the same cycle. It also clears before_abort, which is the scope event R.

Relation R, which holds by construction:
- phase==ARMED implies arm_seen.
- phase is RUN or FIN implies arm_seen and start_seen.
- done implies phase==FIN.
- start_seen implies arm_seen.

Property P (chain precedence, before abort, $rose edge style). The antecedents are before_abort and $rose(done):
  assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) before_abort && $rose(done) |-> arm_seen && start_seen && phase==FIN);
In words: while no abort has ever happened, whenever the finish flag rises, the arm and start steps must already have been recorded.

Counterexample to induction, which satisfies P but violates R:
- phase=RUN, arm_seen=0, start_seen=0, done=0.
- col_cnt=23, row_cnt=7, before_abort=1, with arbitrary char_mem and frame_cnt.
- P holds vacuously in this state because done does not rise.
- The state can be held indefinitely with en=0, since every register holds and done stays 0. This defeats k-induction for any depth k.

One step with en=1 and abort_req=0 moves the design to phase=FIN with done=1. That makes $rose(done) true while arm_seen=0 and start_seen=0, so P is violated. description:
What it is: SPI chip-select sequencer: Asserts and deasserts individual slave-select lines with programmable setup, hold and inter-transfer delays, keeping a selected-slave register, a delay counter and a sequencing state register.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module toast_spi_cs_seq: a memory-mapped SPI chip-select sequencer peripheral, as a Toast RV32I core would expose over MMIO. Software pushes transfer descriptors into a 24-entry queue. Each descriptor holds a 5-bit slave index (0..23) and a 128-bit data word. The sequencer pops a descriptor, asserts that slave's select line, waits a programmable setup delay, then shifts out 128 bits. It then waits a hold delay, deasserts the select line, and waits an inter-transfer gap.

Inputs: clk, rst, en (when en is low every state register holds its value), push, push_slv[4:0], push_data[127:0], and the delay registers cfg_setup[7:0], cfg_hold[7:0], cfg_gap[7:0].

State registers:
- st[2:0]: IDLE, SETUP, XFER, HOLD, GAP.
- sel[4:0]: the selected slave.
- dly[7:0]: delay counter.
- bitcnt[6:0]: shift counter.
- cs_vec[23:0]: active-high select lines; the output is cs_n = ~cs_vec.
- shreg[127:0]: shift register.
- Queue: q_slv[0:23][4:0], q_dat[0:23][127:0], wptr[4:0], rptr[4:0], count[4:0] (24 entries, so the pointers wrap at 23).

Behaviour (all updates only when en is high):
- In IDLE or at the end of GAP, if count != 0: pop the head entry, set sel to q_slv[rptr], set cs_vec <= cs_vec | (24'b1 << q_slv[rptr]), load shreg and set dly <= cfg_setup, then go to SETUP.
- SETUP counts dly down to 0, then goes to XFER with bitcnt = 127.
- XFER shifts one bit per cycle until bitcnt reaches 0, then goes to HOLD with dly = cfg_hold.
- At the end of HOLD: cs_vec <= cs_vec & ~(24'b1 << sel), dly <= cfg_gap, then go to GAP.
- When GAP expires with an empty queue, go to IDLE.
- Reset clears everything.

The select update is a read-modify-write of cs_vec rather than a fresh one-hot assignment. This is why the invariant is only maintained by construction and is not locally evident.

Relation R (holds by construction):
- When st is SETUP, XFER or HOLD: cs_vec == (24'b1 << sel) and sel < 24.
- When st is IDLE or GAP: cs_vec == 24'b0.

Property P (absence of two simultaneous slave selects, global, guarded):
always @(posedge clk) if (st != ST_IDLE) assert ($onehot0(cs_vec));

Counterexample to induction (satisfies P, violates R):
- st = GAP, dly = 1, sel = 5, cs_vec = 24'h000008 (bit 3 stale), count = 1, and q_slv[rptr] = 7.
- P holds, because cs_vec is onehot0.
- R is violated, because cs_vec should be 0 in GAP.
- With en low this state is held indefinitely, so a k-induction prefix of any length satisfies P.
- When en rises, dly reaches 0, the queue pops slave 7, and st moves to SETUP with cs_vec = 24'h000088.
- Two select lines are now asserted with st != IDLE, so P fails.

Giving the prover R excludes the stale bit, and P then becomes inductive.

2. A trace subsystem is added to toast_spi_cs_seq. Each launched frame posts one record into an 8-entry record FIFO.

added: A new sub-module wake_alloc_q (instance u_aq) now sits in front of the matrix's alloc input.
description:
What it is: Dependency matrix wakeup unit: Wakes waiting instructions when their producers issue by consulting a matrix of producer-consumer dependency bits, keeping the dependency matrix and per-entry pending-source flags.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
PicoSoC-themed issue-queue wakeup unit 'pico_wakeup': a 32-entry dependency-matrix scheduler for a small RISC-V core on a Mimas-style board.

Inputs: clk, rst_n, en (idle/enable: when low, every state register holds), alloc, alloc_deps[31:0] (the producer entries the new instruction waits on), issue, issue_idx[4:0].

State registers:
- valid[31:0]: entry-occupied bits.
- dep[0:31][31:0]: dependency matrix. dep[i][j]=1 means consumer i waits on producer j.
- pend[31:0]: per-entry pending-source flags.
- occ[63:0]: occupancy counter.
- wake_cnt[63:0]: free-running count of wakeup events, used as a status register.

Behavior (only when en=1; reset clears everything):
- full = &valid. This is computed from the valid bits, not from occ.
- Allocation fires when alloc && !full. It picks the lowest free index f, sets valid[f], loads dep[f] = alloc_deps & valid, and sets pend[f] = |(alloc_deps & valid).
- Issue fires when issue && valid[issue_idx] && !pend[issue_idx]. It clears valid[issue_idx] and clears column issue_idx in every row of dep. Each entry whose row becomes zero gets its pend bit cleared, and wake_cnt increments by the number of entries woken.
- occ update: occ + 1 on allocation only, occ - 1 on issue only, unchanged when both fire or neither fires.

Relation R (holds by construction):
- occ == $countones(valid).
- For all i: pend[i] == |dep[i].
- For all i: if !valid[i] then dep[i] == 0.

Property P (bounded existence, at most 32, global, guarded style):
always @(posedge clk) if (|valid) assert (occ <= 64'd32);
The bound 32 is far below the 2^64 range of occ, so P is a real fact about reachable states. It holds only because occ tracks the valid popcount and allocation is blocked by full.

Counterexample to induction (CTI):
- The state is valid = 32'h7FFF_FFFF (31 entries occupied), occ = 32, dep = 0, pend = 0.
- P holds, since valid is nonzero and 32 <= 32.
- R is violated, since popcount(valid) = 31 but occ = 32.
- With en=0 this state is held unchanged for any number of cycles, so k-induction cannot rule it out by depth alone.
- Step: raise en=1 and alloc=1 with issue=0. Since full=0, entry 31 is allocated, valid becomes 32'hFFFF_FFFF and occ becomes 33.
- The guard |valid is true, so occ <= 32 fails and P is violated.

Supplying R as a lemma excludes this state. Under R, occ = 32 implies full = 1, so allocation is blocked and occ can never exceed 32. P then becomes inductive.

Inputs: clk, rst_n, en (idle/enable: when low, every state register holds), alloc, alloc_deps[31:0] (the producer entries the new instruction waits on), issue, issue_idx[4:0].

State registers:
- valid[31:0]: entry-occupied bits.
- dep[0:31][31:0]: dependency matrix. dep[i][j]=1 means consumer i waits on producer j.
- pend[31:0]: per-entry pending-source flags.
- occ[63:0]: occupancy counter.
- wake_cnt[63:0]: free-running count of wakeup events, used as a status register.

Behavior (only when en=1; reset clears everything):
- full = &valid. This is computed from the valid bits, not from occ.
- Allocation fires when alloc && !full. It picks the lowest free index f, sets valid[f], loads dep[f] = alloc_deps & valid, and sets pend[f] = |(alloc_deps & valid).
- Issue fires when issue && valid[issue_idx] && !pend[issue_idx]. It clears valid[issue_idx] and clears column issue_idx in every row of dep. Each entry whose row becomes zero gets its pend bit cleared, and wake_cnt increments by the number of entries woken.

- occ == $countones(valid).
- For all i: pend[i] == |dep[i].
- For all i: if !valid[i] then dep[i] == 0.

The bound 32 is far below the 2^64 range of occ, so P is a real fact about reachable states. It holds only because occ tracks the valid popcount and allocation is blocked by full.

- P holds, since valid is nonzero and 32 <= 32.
- R is violated, since popcount(valid) = 31 but occ = 32.

- Step: raise en=1 and alloc=1 with issue=0. Since full=0, entry 31 is allocated, valid becomes 32'hFFFF_FFFF and occ becomes 33.

A feature it must have: valid/ready handshake: give the main input or the main output a valid/ready handshake with back-pressure: an item moves only on a cycle when valid and ready are both high; as the sender, the design holds valid and its data steady until the item moves; as the receiver, it lowers ready when it cannot take more instead of dropping data. With the incoming valid and ready held low nothing moves: that is the idle condition.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. Add a four-entry RGB ingress FIFO submodule with three byte arrays, first/last metadata, read/write pointers, an occupancy counter, and an accepted-pixel telemetry counter. Its head replaces the direct converter input, and its ready output drives i_ready.
2. Adds 98 lines of live telemetry logic: saturating traffic counters, stall tracking, an inactivity watchdog, a FIFO high-water mark, and sticky event flags. All telemetry is observable through the new registered debug_status port, selected by cfg_addr.
3. A feeds B through a four-entry elastic FIFO that packs {Y,Cb,Cr} into meaningful 24-bit pixel words for 4-by-4 transposed tiles.
4. Adds a four-entry analytics work FIFO containing converted pixels and their tile positions, wrap-bit read/write pointers, a worker cursor, a two-phase pixel-analysis stage, and tile-summary accumulators and outputs.

added: A four-entry peer command FIFO holds independently supplied operands and latency. Its pointers, peer_active, peer_phase, and peer_remaining implement a second execution lane.
description:
What it is: NTT butterfly unit: Performs Cooley-Tukey/Gentleman-Sande butterflies modulo a small prime for lattice-based post-quantum schemes such as Kyber and Dilithium, holding coefficient operand registers, the current twiddle factor and stage/index counters.
A feature it must have: valid/ready handshake and a register loaded from an input: give the main input or the main output a valid/ready handshake with back-pressure: an item moves only on a cycle when valid and ready are both high; as the sender, the design holds valid and its data steady until the item moves; as the receiver, it lowers ready when it cannot take more instead of dropping data. With the incoming valid and ready held low nothing moves: that is the idle condition. Also load one register from an input port - a limit, a starting value or a configuration - at reset or when a load command is high, so its value is not fixed and the property and the invariants must hold for every value it can take; it still gets an initial value, which a load replaces, and it keeps its value between loads, including while the design idles.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. A four-entry parameterized command FIFO adds q_a, q_b, q_w, q_lat, wrap-bit pointers q_wr/q_rd, and head_valid. Enqueue captures operands and normalized latency.
2. A new ntt_phase_dispatch submodule adds four programmable burst profiles, a configuration transaction sequencer, a configuration write cursor, pending and normalized configuration words, an active quantum, and a scheduled phase step.
3. A four-entry peer command FIFO holds independently supplied operands and latency. Its pointers, peer_active, peer_phase, and peer_remaining implement a second execution lane.

added: Add a UART word-formatting subunit with an eight-symbol frame array, a symbol index, a frame span, and an IDLE/SEND/WAIT/DONE controller. Address zero retains raw-byte transmission; writes to address 0x0008 transmit ':HHHHCC\n', containing four hexadecimal payload digits and a CRC-8.
description:
What it is: AXI clock-domain crossing bridge: Carries all five AXI channels between asynchronous clock domains using per-channel dual-clock storage, holding the payload memories plus write and read pointers on each side.
A feature it must have: a register loaded from an input: load one register from an input port - a limit, a starting value or a configuration - at reset or when a load command is high, so its value is not fixed and the property and the invariants must hold for every value it can take; it still gets an initial value, which a load replaces, and it keeps its value between loads, including while the design idles.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. A's 16-bit write FIFO feeds B configured with DATA_W=8 through an address/data join and register decoder: writes to address zero transmit the low byte, unsupported addresses receive DECERR, and the bridge's ready path stalls until the address, response capacity and UART are available.
2. Add a UART word-formatting subunit with an eight-symbol frame array, a symbol index, a frame span, and an IDLE/SEND/WAIT/DONE controller. Address zero retains raw-byte transmission; writes to address 0x0008 transmit ':HHHHCC\n', containing four hexadecimal payload digits and a CRC-8.

description:
What it is: Color space converter: Applies a fixed matrix transform between color representations, keeping coefficient registers and an optional output pipeline register.
A feature it must have: valid/ready handshake: give the main input or the main output a valid/ready handshake with back-pressure: an item moves only on a cycle when valid and ready are both high; as the sender, the design holds valid and its data steady until the item moves; as the receiver, it lowers ready when it cannot take more instead of dropping data. With the incoming valid and ready held low nothing moves: that is the idle condition.
Then grown in steps; each step added:
1. Add a four-entry RGB ingress FIFO submodule with three byte arrays, first/last metadata, read/write pointers, an occupancy counter, and an accepted-pixel telemetry counter. Its head replaces the direct converter input, and its ready output drives i_ready.
2. Adds 98 lines of live telemetry logic: saturating traffic counters, stall tracking, an inactivity watchdog, a FIFO high-water mark, and sticky event flags. All telemetry is observable through the new registered debug_status port, selected by cfg_addr.
3. A feeds B through a four-entry elastic FIFO that packs {Y,Cb,Cr} into meaningful 24-bit pixel words for 4-by-4 transposed tiles.
4. Adds a parameterized posted-configuration FIFO containing address, data, and an accepted-pixel watermark, wrap-bit read/write pointers, a command execution stage, and an acknowledged completion mailbox.

Also name the states of the design's controller with typedef enum, declared inside the module with an explicit width, such as typedef enum logic [1:0] {IDLE, BUSY, DONE} state_t; give the state register an initial value, write the state names, not numbers, in the logic, the property and the invariants, and if the width allows codes no state uses, include an invariant ruling them out, as for any unreachable value.

What it is: Universal shift register: Holds a data word that can be loaded in parallel, shifted left, shifted right, or held according to mode inputs.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module cnn_act_shreg: an 8-bit activation-scaling universal shift register for a MicroCNN datapath. A quantized pixel or activation is parallel-loaded, then shifted left or right to rescale it (logical shifts, zero fill). Bit 7 drives out_sat, a saturation flag to the next layer.

Inputs: clk, rst, en (when low, all state holds), mode[1:0] (00 hold, 01 shift left, 10 shift right, 11 load), din[7:0], flush.

State registers:
- win[7:0]: the data word, reset to 0.
- cnt[7:0]: saturating count of loads.
- loaded (1 bit): shadow, reset 0; set when en && mode==11 && din!=0; never cleared.
- pristine (1 bit): reset 1; cleared on the first en && flush.

Update rule: when en is high, flush sets win to 0 and has priority over mode; otherwise win follows mode. Because shifts insert only zeros, a 1 can enter win only through a nonzero parallel load.

Relation R (holds by construction): (win != 0) -> loaded.

Property P (precedence, before-flush scope, $rose style): pristine && $rose(win[7]) |-> loaded. In words: while no flush has ever happened, whenever the saturation bit rises, a nonzero activation must have been loaded earlier.

Induction counterexample (CTI): win=8'h40, loaded=0, pristine=1, cnt=0.
- It satisfies P, since win[7]=0 and nothing rises.
- It violates R, since win is nonzero but loaded is 0.
- It is held unchanged indefinitely with en=0, giving an arbitrarily long P-satisfying prefix.
- Then with en=1, mode=01, flush=0, win becomes 8'h80. win[7] rises while loaded stays 0 and pristine stays 1, so P is violated.

With R supplied as a strengthening invariant, k-induction (k=1) proves P.

What it is: Single-port SRAM wrapper: Wraps a memory macro with address, data, and enable registers for one access per cycle.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
hyperram_burst_sram: single-port SRAM wrapper (mem[0:7], 32-bit words) that serves HyperRAM-style read or write bursts, one word access per cycle. State registers: mode (2-bit: 0=idle, 1=read burst, 2=write burst), own_rd (1-bit), own_wr (1-bit), cnt (32-bit beats remaining), addr_q (3-bit), data_q (32-bit), win (1-bit), mem (8x32). Input en: when low, all state holds, including mem and win. Behaviour when en=1: if mode==0 and rd_req, then mode<=1, own_rd<=1, cnt<=len. Otherwise if mode==0 and wr_req, then mode<=2, own_wr<=1, cnt<=len. Each beat increments addr_q, decrements cnt, and reads or writes mem[addr_q] through data_q. When cnt reaches 1, mode<=0 and the active owner flag clears. A start only sets its own flag and never touches the other flag. Window: cfg_lock (Q, the latency-config write) sets win; cfg_unlock (R) clears it; cfg_unlock may never arrive. Relation R (holds by construction): own_rd==(mode==1) && own_wr==(mode==2). P (absence, after Q until R): always @(posedge clk) assert (!(win && own_rd && own_wr)); win is the window register in the antecedent. Counterexample to induction: win=1, mode=0, own_rd=1, own_wr=0, cnt=0. This state satisfies P but violates R (mode is idle while own_rd is set). It is held unchanged while en=0. On the next step with en=1 and wr_req=1, mode==0 allows a write start, so own_wr<=1 while own_rd stays 1, violating P. With R as a helper lemma, mode==0 forces both owner flags to 0, so P becomes inductive.
What it is: Modular exponentiation engine: Performs square-and-multiply exponentiation over a modulus, holding base, running result, exponent shift register, and bit counter.

What it is: Keccak-f permutation core: Executes the theta, rho, pi, chi and iota steps of the Keccak-f[1600] permutation for SHA-3 and SHAKE, keeping the 5x5 lane state array and a round index counter.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module lut_keccak_rng: a reduced Keccak-style permutation core that whitens a 128-bit seed into stochastic bitstreams for LUT-network training. It runs 24 rounds of theta/rho/pi/chi/iota-like steps on one 128-bit word. The word is viewed as 4x32 lanes. Each round does the following, in order: theta XORs in column parity; rho/pi rotate the lanes and permute their order; chi computes s ^ (~rotl(s,1) & rotl(s,2)); iota XORs RC[rnd]. RC is a constant 24-entry ROM of 128-bit words.

Ports: clk, rst, en (when en is low, all state holds), arm, start, seed[127:0], q_open, r_close; outputs done, out[127:0].

State registers:
- st[127:0]: permutation state.
- rnd[4:0]: round index, 0..23.
- phase[1:0]: IDLE=0, ARMED=1, RUNNING=2, DONE=3.
- armed_seen and started_seen: 1 bit each.
- win: 1-bit window register.

Behavior when en is high:
- IDLE and arm: go to ARMED and set armed_seen.
- ARMED and start: go to RUNNING, set started_seen, set rnd=0 and load st=seed.
- RUNNING: apply one round and increment rnd. When rnd==23, go to DONE.
- DONE: assert done, then return to IDLE and clear both seen flags.
- Window: win is set by q_open and cleared by r_close (r_close has priority). It can open and close any number of times.

Relation R (holds by construction):
- phase==IDLE implies !armed_seen && !started_seen.
- phase>=ARMED implies armed_seen.
- phase>=RUNNING implies started_seen.
- phase!=RUNNING implies rnd==0.
- rnd<=23 always.

Property P (chain precedence arm, then start, then finish, scoped between q_open and r_close):
always @(posedge clk) if (win && phase==2'd3) assert (armed_seen && started_seen);

Counterexample to induction: win=1, phase=RUNNING, rnd=23, armed_seen=1, started_seen=0, st arbitrary.
- It satisfies P, since phase is not DONE.
- It violates R, since phase is RUNNING but started_seen is 0.
- It can be held forever with en=0, so any induction depth k admits it.
- With en=1 and r_close=0, it steps to phase=DONE with started_seen=0 inside the window, which violates P.

Supplying R as a lemma excludes this state and makes P k-inductive.

What it is: Rounding unit: Applies a selected rounding mode to a truncated result using guard, round, and sticky bits stored in a small status register.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module rnd_unit_win: a windowed rounding unit with a 128-entry log. Each cycle with en=1 it takes a 64-bit truncated mantissa trunc_in, a 3-bit guard/round/sticky input grs_in and a 2-bit mode (00 RNE, 01 RTZ, 10 RUP, 11 RDN, with sign_in). When en=0, every register holds.

State registers:
- stat_q[5:0]: status register holding {grs, mode, sign}.
- res_q[63:0]: rounded result. It is trunc + 1 when the round-up decision is taken, otherwise trunc.
- log_mem[0:127][63:0]: result log.
- wr_ptr[6:0]: log write pointer.
- up_cnt[63:0]: round-up events in the current window.
- dn_cnt[63:0]: truncate (no-increment) events in the current window.

Round-up decision rup:
- RNE: g & (r | s | lsb).
- RUP: (g|r|s) & ~sign.
- RDN: (g|r|s) & sign.
- RTZ: 0.

Update on en=1:
- Write res into log_mem[wr_ptr] and increment wr_ptr.
- Statistics window of 100 operations: if up_cnt + dn_cnt == 99 (compare at 65 bits), the current op closes the window and both counters clear to 0.
- Otherwise, if rup then up_cnt++, else dn_cnt++.
- Reset: everything is 0.

Relation R (holds by construction): up_cnt + dn_cnt <= 99, using a 65-bit sum. It holds because each enabled step either raises the sum by exactly 1 from at most 98, or clears both counters when the sum equals 99.

Property P: two global assertions, checked in every reachable state with no arming register.
- A1: up_cnt <= 99.
- A2: dn_cnt <= 99.
Both bounds are far below 2^64. Neither assertion is inductive alone, because each says nothing about the other counter. With R as a lemma, both follow immediately (up_cnt <= up_cnt + dn_cnt <= 99, and likewise for dn_cnt). R is itself inductive, so it closes both.

Counterexample to induction without R:
- State: up_cnt = 99, dn_cnt = 1, other registers arbitrary.
- It satisfies A1 and A2, since both values are <= 99.
- It violates R, since the sum is 100.
- With en=0 it is held indefinitely, so k-induction of any depth can stay in it.
- Step with en=1, mode=RUP, sign_in=0, grs_in=3'b100 (so rup=1). The sum is 100, not 99, so the window does not close, and up_cnt becomes 100, violating A1.
- Symmetrically, the state up_cnt = 1, dn_cnt = 99 stepped with mode=RTZ gives dn_cnt = 100, violating A2.

Both assertions therefore need the same planted relation R.

What it is: Dirty-bit tracking RAM: A RAM that sets a per-block dirty flag whenever any word in that block is written so software can find modified regions; it keeps the data array and a dirty-bit array.
The designer's plan, written before the code:
Module: ckpt_dirty_ram, a relocatable-module tile cache in the spirit of RapidWright's pre-implemented module checkpoints. Software checkpoints the tile store, writes words, then scans dirty blocks to find tiles that must be re-relocated and written back.

Inputs: clk, rst, en (when low, all state holds), we, addr[6:0], wdata[7:0], ckpt (Q), release (R).

State registers:
- mem[0:127][7:0]: data array of 128 8-bit words, organized as 16 blocks of 8 words, with blk = addr[6:3].
- dirty[15:0]: one dirty bit per block.
- clean[7:0]: count of blocks still clean since the last checkpoint. This is the shadow of the earlier checkpoint event.
- win (1 bit): window register.

Behavior (all updates only when en is high; rst sets dirty=0, clean=16, win=0):
- If ckpt: dirty <= 0, clean <= 16, win <= 1. ckpt has priority, so a write in the same cycle is ignored.
- Else if release: win <= 0.
- If we and not ckpt:
  - mem[addr] <= wdata;
  - dirty[blk] <= 1;
  - if (!dirty[blk] && clean != 0), clean <= clean - 1.
- release and a write may occur in the same cycle.

Relation R (holds by construction): clean == 16 - popcount(dirty). Consequently, clean == 0 exactly when all 16 dirty bits are set.

Property P (precedence, after ckpt until release, $stable style): any change in the dirty set must be preceded by the clean counter recording it. Inside an open window, if the clean count did not change, no dirty bit changed.
  assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (rst) (win && $past(win) && $stable(clean)) |-> $stable(dirty));
The window is set by ckpt and cleared only by release, which may never arrive. P must therefore hold for the whole time after a checkpoint. win appears in the antecedent.

Why P is true: under R, a write to a clean block always finds clean != 0. So dirty and clean change together. A write to an already-dirty block changes neither.

Counterexample to induction (CTI) without R: take the state win=1, clean=0, dirty=16'h7FFF (block 15 clean). This violates R, because the actual count of clean blocks is 1.
- Holding en=0 keeps this state forever. Both $stable checks are true, so P holds across any induction depth.
- Then assert en=1, we=1, addr=7'h78 (block 15), with ckpt=0 and release=0.
- Because clean==0, the guard blocks the decrement and clean stays 0, while dirty becomes 16'hFFFF.
- In the next cycle, win && $past(win) && $stable(clean) holds but $stable(dirty) fails, so P is violated.

Supplying R as a helper invariant rules out the state. With R, clean==0 forces dirty==16'hFFFF, and then P is k-inductive.
